successCriteria.description: ApprovalsPage renders a table whose rows show: Employee as employeeId truncated to its first 8 characters in a monospace style (no name resolution), Leave type as leaveTypeCode, Start and End formatted via formatUtcDate, and a link to /leaves/{requestId}.
A short user-facing note (e.g. "employee names require an API change") is visible near the Employee column — rendered text, not a code TODO comment.

Each queue row shows Approve and Reject buttons that call approvalsService.decide(requestId, 'approve'|'reject'); on success the row's data is replaced with the returned LeaveRequestView (new status rendered, approve/reject controls removed) without removing the row and without re-fetching the list.

The page renders three mutually distinct states: an explicit empty state ("nothing waiting on you") when getQueue() resolves to [], a loading state while the fetch is in flight, and an error state with role="alert" when getQueue() rejects.
App.tsx adds a /approvals route wrapped in RequireAuth and RequireApprover rendering ApprovalsPage with approvalsService, and AppProps gains approvalsService: IApprovalsService (destructured).
The composition root constructs ApprovalsService(leaveService, employeeService) and passes it to App, and ApprovalsPage is exported from web/src/presentation/index.ts.

constraints: ApprovalsPage must receive IApprovalsService via a prop (imported from web/src/modules/approvals/index.ts); it must not import the api-client or construct the service itself.
The Employee column must render employeeId truncated to its first 8 characters in a monospace style; do NOT attempt name resolution (employeeName is always null).
On a successful decide, replace the row's data with the returned LeaveRequestView (render new status, remove approve/reject controls); do NOT remove the row and do NOT re-fetch the whole list.
The "employee names require an API change" note must be user-facing rendered text, not a TODO comment in code.
The /approvals route must be wrapped in both RequireAuth and RequireApprover; role is read from the auth session profile, never decoded from the JWT.
Dates must be formatted with formatUtcDate from web/src/shared/date/index.ts (no ad-hoc date formatting).
outOfScope: Employee name resolution (employeeName is always null; the note explicitly flags this as requiring an API change).
ApprovalsPage test suite and the role-gated dashboard link (Phase 5).
Any change to the approvals service, leave service, or API contract (getQueue/decide already exist from Phase 1).

entityInvariants.invariant: A queue item is a derived read-model projection, never persisted; while in the queue its status is always LeaveStatus.SUBMITTED and employeeName is always null. It is consumed read-only by ApprovalsPage and never mutated by the page.
The value returned by decide() is the authoritative post-decision state; the page must render its status verbatim and must not derive or guess a new status locally.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Caller must be authenticated; role gating is enforced by the RequireApprover guard on the route, not by the service.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Rejections from getMe()/list() propagate to the caller; the page surfaces them as the error state (role="alert").

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Caller must be authenticated and an approver (MANAGER/ADMIN); enforced by the route guard.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: On failure the rejection propagates and the page surfaces the error state; on success the returned LeaveRequestView replaces the row.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Follow the LeaveDetailPage async pattern: useState for data/error, useEffect with a cancelled flag for the initial fetch, async action handler that updates state on success or sets error on failure, role="alert" for errors, and a "Loading…" state while data is null.
Use formatUtcDate for Start/End date rendering.
Import LeaveStatus, LeaveTypeCode, LeaveRequestView from the shared types module; do not redeclare them.
Import IApprovalsService from the approvals module public entry point.
Wrap the /approvals route with RequireApprover (which already handles null-session redirect to /login and EMPLOYEE redirect to /).
Detail links must target /leaves/{requestId}, matching the existing /leaves/:id route.

integrationPoints.why: ApprovalsPage consumes getQueue()/decide() through this interface; the page must not reach into the api-client.
Must construct ApprovalsService(leaveService, employeeService) and pass it to App; required follow-up wiring edit in this phase.
ApprovalsPage (and its props type) must be exported so App/main can import it.
